report:
Reviewed the complete region_excerpts claim, sole ordinary implementation association in evidence.rs, ordinary nested_regions_close_the_nearest_opener_and_points_keep_their_own_preview test, and todo::nested_region_excerpts. Verified historical test source snapshots exactly match both current test files; implementation differs only by an unrelated meta.reviews.decisions association comment. Independently inspected current behavior and assertions rather than inheriting the prior verdict.

marker accepts an immediate << suffix as a region; index_source creates a fresh open stack for each source file, pushes only region references and pops the nearest opener only for standalone // >> comments. Thus regions nest within a file, and point references neither close nor replace open regions. Lines::start/end and closing-line assignment include both marker lines in each excerpt. The ordinary test constructs nested regions with a point inside, requires no diagnostics, checks region flags, outer 1..7, inner 3..5, point 4..9, exact outer/inner excerpts and point span slicing through the final line. These assertions would detect wrong nesting, excluded delimiters, and a point that prematurely terminated or replaced an open region. The captured index helper passes the literal fixture to CorrespondenceIndex::from_sources; substantive assertions remain visible in the test body. Standalone closure and per-file isolation additionally follow directly from the captured scanner and per-invocation stack.

Access/navigation to surrounding source remains explicitly deferred by todo::nested_region_excerpts. Its empty body is not substantive coverage. Its boundary/nesting/point portions already have ordinary coverage; the outstanding prerequisite is a source-navigation integration fixture exposing a region excerpt with its surrounding source, followed by navigation assertions. This retains the previous justified TODO rationale and does not assert browser behavior is complete. No N/A entries exist, and no edits are requested.

Execution: personally ran review start, review read and snapshot comparison commands; no behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator separately reports 321 passing sage-meta tests and a passing root build; that report is execution context, not personal verification. This verdict is source adequacy review with explicit deferred navigation coverage.
